title: Kris Kringle Ideas for Work and Family | Albums.ink
desc: Kris Kringle ideas for an Aussie Christmas: budgets, twists for adults, a fair draw – and one QR code that gathers everyone’s photos of the gift swap.
h1: Kris Kringle ideas for work and family
lead: In Australia, Google suggests “kris kringle ideas with a twist”, “for adults”, “$30” and “$50” as soon as you start typing. Kris Kringle is the local name for Secret Santa: everyone draws one name and buys one gift. Here is how to run a smooth draw, a few twists for adults, and a simple way to keep the photos of the big reveal.
body: ## Set the rules early
- Budget: pick one number and stick to it – $20, $30 or $50 are the amounts Australians search for most.
- The draw: names in a hat at morning tea, or an online name generator if the team works hybrid.
- Wish lists: ask everyone for one or two hints (a hobby, a favourite snack, “no candles please”).
- Date: hold it at the last team lunch before the Christmas break or at the family Christmas Eve get-together.
## Kris Kringle with a twist
- Steal (Yankee swap): gifts are opened in turn and anyone can steal one already unwrapped.
- Theme: “something Australian”, “something for summer”, “something under $30 from an op shop”.
- Guess the giver: everyone has one guess before the giver is revealed.
- Kids’ Kris Kringle: a separate draw for the cousins so adults only buy one gift each.
## Keep the photos of the reveal
Half the fun is the faces when the gifts are opened – and those photos end up on ten different phones. An event album on Albums puts them in one place:
1. Create the album, e.g. “Office Kris Kringle 2026”.
2. Print the QR code and stick it on the gift table, or post it in the team chat.
3. Guests scan it with their phone camera and upload photos and videos from the browser – nothing to install.
4. Turn on Hold guest photos if you want to approve uploads first (useful at work).
5. In January, download the whole album as one ZIP file.
Guests who upload without signing in appear anonymously. Signed-in guests also get a private draft copy with only their own uploads.

faq: What is Kris Kringle in Australia?
The Australian name for Secret Santa: each person draws one name and buys a gift for that person within an agreed budget.
How much should you spend on Kris Kringle?
Whatever the group agrees on; $20, $30 and $50 are common limits.
Do guests need to install anything to share photos?
No. They scan the QR code and upload from the browser.
How long are the photos kept?
6 months from the first upload, and the album can be extended.
